back: The period and practices by which two unmarried people get to know each other, with a view to marriage.

front: Name three meeting places of indigenous courtship.
back: Any three of: the river or well, the fields, work parties (nhimbe/ilima), village dances, the path to the fields.

front: Who advised a girl about a suitor in indigenous courtship?
Who advised a young man during indigenous courtship?
What did a token such as beads (chuma) show in indigenous courtship?
back: That the young woman had accepted the young man's proposal.

front: Name four forms of contemporary courtship.
back: Social, religious, western-influenced and online courtship.

front: Why were totems checked in indigenous courtship?
back: To make sure the couple were not of the same clan, because marriage between close relatives was forbidden.

front: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of contemporary courtship.
back: Advantage: free choice by the couple. Disadvantage: fewer family checks, so deception (especially online) is easier.

front: How can a young person combine modern courtship with indigenous safeguards?
back: Choose freely, but tell a trusted aunt, uncle or parent and let the family meet the partner before the relationship becomes serious.
